Overview
Nightfood Holdings was incorporated
on October 16, 2013, in the State of Nevada in connection with a reorganization of Nightfood, Inc., incorporated on January 14, 2010
as a New York corporation, whereby it became the first wholly-owned subsidiary of Nightfood Holdings. We are also the sole
shareholder of MJ Munchies, Inc., currently revoked in the State of Nevada, which owns certain intellectual property, but does not
have any operations as of the period covered by these financial statements.
Nightfood Holdings operates through five wholly owned
subsidiaries that collectively position us to capitalize on the accelerating demand for automation and efficiency in the hospitality and
foodservice industries: TechForce Robotics, Inc. (formerly Skytech Automated Solutions Inc.), Future Hospitality Ventures Holdings Inc.
(d/b/a RoboOp365), SWC Group, Inc. (d/b/a CarryOutSupplies.com), Victorville Treasure Holdings, LLC and Treasure Mountain Holdings, LLC.
Treasure Mountain Holdings, LLC is a hotel located at 71700 Highway 111,
Rancho Mirage, California 92270. This property is owned by the Company as of September 30, 2025. Both hotel properties are encumbered
by the mortgage notes payable described in Note 5 to the consolidated financial statements.
TechForce Robotics, Inc., or TechForce or Skytech,
a Delaware corporation which we acquired on March 31, 2025, serves as the Company’s operational backbone, supported by a team with
deep expertise in hospitality operations and a proven track record of building, managing, and scaling hotel and foodservice platforms.
This operational strength enables TechForce to lead to the deployment of robotic and AI-enhanced automation solutions, ensuring seamless
integration into daily operations. Management believes Skytech’s depth of experience is a key differentiator that positions the
Company to execute where many robotics competitors may struggle.
Future Hospitality Ventures Holdings Inc., or FHVH,
Ventures Holdings or Future Hospitality, a Nevada corporation which we acquired on February 2, 2024, enhances this foundation by delivering
advanced AI-enabled robotic systems designed to reduce labor costs, increase efficiency, and improve consumer experience. Launched in
California shortly before the state’s 2025 minimum wage increase in foodservice and hospitality, Ventures Holdings has benefited
from heightened industry awareness and urgency around automation. Its plug-and-play solutions are designed to integrate easily into restaurants,
hotels, healthcare facilities, school cafeterias, and other foodservice environments, with exponential benefits for operators managing
multiple locations is our initial strategic focus.
SWC Group, Inc., or SWC, a California
corporation which we acquired on March 31, 2025, further complements the Company’s ecosystem, having served more than 6,000
foodservice operators across the United States. As a recognized leader in custom-printed foodservice packaging, SWC generates
recurring revenue while also providing a ready-made distribution and marketing channel for cross-selling our robotic solutions to an
established base of industry decision-makers.
On August 27, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition
of the Holiday Inn Victorville, a 155-room hotel property, through an all-equity transaction valued at approximately $39.0 million (excluding
contingent consideration of $7.13 million), consisting of the issuance of 216,667 shares of the Company’s Series C Convertible Preferred
Stock. This property is one of two hotel assets recently acquired by the Company and is intended to support the Company’s operational
presence in the hospitality sector and facilitate evaluation of its robotic solutions within an operating hotel environment.
On September 30, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition
of Rancho Mirage Hilton LLC, the owner of the Hilton Garden Inn Palm Springs - Rancho Mirage, for total consideration of approximately
$42.28 million (excluding contingent consideration of $4.8 million), which was satisfied through the issuance of 176,167 shares of Series
C Convertible Preferred Stock.
The hotel properties support the Company’s hospitality operations and provide operating environments for evaluating and demonstrating
its robotic solutions. Both properties are encumbered by the mortgage notes payable described in Note 5 to the consolidated financial
statements.

Recent
development
On September 17, 2026, the Company announced the formation
of TechForce Advanced Manufacturing, Inc. (“TAMI”), a Nevada corporation established to support the Company’s planned
expansion into the semiconductor manufacturing equipment industry. As of October 12, 2026, the Company is negotiating an agreement to
acquire specified intellectual property and technology assets from JUN LONG MACHINE INDUSTRIAL CO., LTD. (“JUN LONG”), a Taiwan
corporation. The definitive agreement has not been finalized or executed, and the proposed transaction has not closed.
Under the structure currently being negotiated, the
Company would acquire technology and intellectual property relating to wafer sorters and automated optical inspection (“AOI”)
systems, including designs, software, firmware, technical documentation, and manufacturing know-how. The Company would own the acquired
assets and grant TAMI an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to manufacture, sell, and support products using the technology. The
proposed transaction is structured solely as an acquisition of specified intellectual property and technology assets.
The proposed acquisition consideration would consist
of shares of the Company’s Series C Convertible Preferred Stock and a 49% equity interest in TAMI issued to JUN LONG, with the Company
retaining a 51% controlling interest. The parties are also negotiating separate, performance-based preferred stock incentives tied to
qualifying revenue from new customers introduced by JUN LONG. The consideration, incentive terms, and other transaction provisions remain
subject to negotiation and final agreement.
TAMI’s initial commercial focus would be the
manufacture and commercialization of wafer sorter and AOI systems for 8-inch and 12-inch silicon wafers, including applications supporting
Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate, Chip-on-Panel-on-Substrate, and other advanced semiconductor packaging technologies. TAMI is expected to
conduct operations in its own name and for its own account, using its own facility and equipment and developing its own workforce. The
Company expects to provide strategic oversight, commercialization support, public-company infrastructure, and funding through intercompany
loans. JUN LONG is expected to provide limited technical support and training under arrangements that remain subject to negotiation.
Subject to execution of definitive agreements, satisfaction
of applicable closing and regulatory requirements, establishment of manufacturing capacity, availability of funding, and customer demand,
the Company is targeting commencement of production and initial revenue during the fourth quarter of calendar 2026. Revenue recognition
would depend on the applicable contractual terms, delivery and acceptance requirements, and U.S. GAAP. There can be no assurance that
the proposed transaction will close or that production or revenue will commence within the targeted period.
Our vision
Looking
ahead, the Company intends to extend its robotics and automation solutions beyond hospitality into other labor-intensive sectors, including
healthcare facilities, convention centers, educational institutions, and large-scale entertainment venues, while also pursuing a planned entry into the semiconductor manufacturing
equipment industry. Through TechForce Advanced Manufacturing, the Company expects to apply its automation, commercialization and public
company capabilities to the development, manufacture, commercialization, installation and support of semiconductor automation and inspection
systems, initially focused on Wafer Sorter and Automated Optical Inspection systems for 8-inch and 12-inch silicon wafers and related
advanced-packaging applications. By combining TechForce’s
operational expertise, Future Hospitality’s advanced AI robotics, SWC’s extensive customer access, our owned hotel assets
as innovation test beds, and JUN LONG’s technical know-how, manufacturing expertise, product development capabilities and customer relationships,
the Company seeks to build a diversified, vertically integrated platform designed to drive innovation, efficiency, and long-term
shareholder value across multiple industries. TechForce Advanced Manufacturing’s initiative remains subject to completion of a definitive agreement and other
applicable commercial, operational and qualification requirements.
